## EMST role: Wildlife biologist (state variant, senior level; P2)

*Match:* `skos:broadMatch`, confidence 0.45, unreviewed agent draft (`emst-x5-tx:R15-wildlife-biologist/state:2684`). *Authority position (editorial):* resource-manager.

**Competency targets at this level (editorial draft target levels, agent-drafted)**

- Capture, handle and mark wildlife and fish humanely and safely — senior L3
- Detect and record wildlife by direct observation, sign and standardized surveys — senior L3
- Assess species habitat requirements and habitat condition — senior L3
- Identify organisms from field characters, specimens, images and recordings — senior L3
- Assess effects on protected species and conduct interagency consultation on proposed actions — senior L3
- Design monitoring and sampling for valid environmental inference — senior L3
- Adjudicate automated species detections using field-formed identification expertise — senior L3
- Analyze environmental data statistically and interpret the results — senior L3
- Assess and monitor biodiversity across species and habitats — senior L3
- Navigate and travel safely in remote terrain with and without digital aids — senior L2
- Implement international wildlife and fisheries conservation agreements — senior L2
- Interpret and question environmental data products in everyday work — senior L1
- Use AI tools responsibly in everyday environmental work — senior L1
- Validate AI-generated work products before professional use — senior L1
- Record provenance and AI involvement in work products — senior L1

**Main tasks at this level (agent draft, in record order)**

*% time: set by the supervisor; EMST supplies none before job analysis.*

*Critical and needed-at-entry tasks: Assessment pending (job analysis).*

- Capture animals with traps, nets or electrofishing following the approved animal-care protocol and permit conditions
- Immobilize an animal chemically where authorized, monitoring vital signs until recovery and recording drug doses
- Mark captured animals with tags or other marks while recording biological data within protocol handling-time and stress limits
- Apply zoonotic disease and personal safety precautions when handling wildlife, including protective equipment and decontamination
- Deploy camera traps and acoustic recorders at survey stations to the protocol's height, orientation and settings, recording station metadata
- Conduct ground or aerial counts of target species along defined survey units to support abundance estimation
- Train seasonal crew members in survey protocol and identification cues, checking each trainee's detections against an experienced observer
- Conduct point-count, transect or call-playback wildlife surveys to protocol, recording detections, distance bands and survey conditions
- Measure habitat attributes such as cover, structure, water and forage at used and available sites following a habitat-use study protocol
- Evaluate a habitat suitability map against field observations of use and condition, documenting where and why the model fails
- Integrate habitat findings into land-use or project plans as specific measures that avoid or reduce effects on species of concern
- Observe animal movement, foraging and breeding behaviour at study sites, recording behaviour and habitat context on standardized forms

## EMST role: Fisheries and aquatic biologist (state variant, senior level; P2)

*Match:* `skos:broadMatch`, confidence 0.5, unreviewed agent draft (`emst-x5-tx:R16-fisheries-aquatic-biologist/state:2684`). *Authority position (editorial):* resource-manager.

**Competency targets at this level (editorial draft target levels, agent-drafted)**

- Manage fish populations and habitats to stated conservation and harvest objectives — senior L3
- Conduct fisheries stock assessments and develop management advice — senior L3
- Capture, handle and mark wildlife and fish humanely and safely — senior L3
- Operate small boats and work safely on water in aquatic, coastal and marine field settings — senior L2
- Measure water quality and survey aquatic communities in the field — senior L3
- Apply field biosecurity and decontamination protocols — senior L2
- Operate fish hatchery and aquatic propagation programmes — senior L2
- Collect trace-level and genetic environmental samples without contamination — senior L2
- Design monitoring and sampling for valid environmental inference — senior L3
- Analyze environmental data statistically and interpret the results — senior L3
- Interpret and question environmental data products in everyday work — senior L1
- Use AI tools responsibly in everyday environmental work — senior L1
- Validate AI-generated work products before professional use — senior L1
- Record provenance and AI involvement in work products — senior L1

**Main tasks at this level (agent draft, in record order)**

*% time: set by the supervisor; EMST supplies none before job analysis.*

*Critical and needed-at-entry tasks: Assessment pending (job analysis).*

- Sample fish populations by electrofishing, netting or hydroacoustics following the survey protocol to estimate abundance and size structure
- Recommend harvest regulations, stocking or habitat actions for a fishery from population assessment results and angler objectives
- Assess water quality and habitat conditions limiting a fish population, identifying the factors management can change
- Estimate age, growth and mortality of a fish population from scale or otolith readings and catch-curve data
- Fit a stock assessment model to catch, survey and biological data, documenting model diagnostics and retrospective patterns
- Apply a data-limited assessment method to a stock with sparse catch and survey data, stating the uncertainty in reference points
- Present assessment results and catch advice to a scientific review panel, answering its requested analyses with documented runs
- Capture animals with traps, nets or electrofishing following the approved animal-care protocol and permit conditions
- Immobilize an animal chemically where authorized, monitoring vital signs until recovery and recording drug doses
- Mark captured animals with tags or other marks while recording biological data within protocol handling-time and stress limits
- Execute person-overboard, capsize and cold-water immersion procedures for a small-boat crew during drills and real events
- Work sampling gear such as grabs, nets, sondes or traps over the side of a small vessel, keeping crew clear of lines and winches

## EMST role: Restoration and land stewardship project lead (state variant, journey/senior level; P1)

*Match:* `skos:broadMatch`, confidence 0.4, unreviewed agent draft (`emst-x5-tx:R09-restoration-project-lead/state:2684`). *Authority position (editorial):* resource-manager.

**Competency targets at this level (editorial draft target levels, agent-drafted)**

- Implement ecological restoration treatments and adapt them to site response — journey L2, senior L3
- Read site history and reference conditions from landscape evidence — journey L2, senior L3
- Assess species habitat requirements and habitat condition — journey L2, senior L3
- Design monitoring and sampling for valid environmental inference — journey L2, senior L3
- Deliver environmental projects to budget, schedule and quality — journey L2, senior L3
- Work alongside landowners, permittees, volunteers and communities on the land — journey L2, senior L3
- Map the decision authority and procedural pathway for a proposed action — journey L2, senior L2
- Administer contracts, grants and intergovernmental agreements — journey L2, senior L3
- Recognize and assess ecosystems that have crossed into novel states — journey L2, senior L3
- Lead field crews and transfer field judgment to novices — journey L2, senior L3
- Plan and run field campaigns and remote logistics — journey L2, senior L3
- Manage client and partner scope for environmental work — journey L2, senior L2
- Develop proposals and grant applications for environmental work — journey L2, senior L2
- Detect, treat and monitor invasive species in the field — journey L2, senior L2
- Install and maintain erosion control and watershed treatments — journey L2, senior L2
- Apply systems thinking across ecological, institutional and technical systems — journey L2, senior L2
- Develop and manage partnerships for shared environmental goals — senior L2
- Manage risk in uncontrolled field environments — journey L2, senior L3
- Interpret and question environmental data products in everyday work — journey L1, senior L1
- Use AI tools responsibly in everyday environmental work — journey L1, senior L1
- Validate AI-generated work products before professional use — journey L1, senior L1
- Record provenance and AI involvement in work products — journey L1, senior L1
- Run the adaptive management cycle and evaluate programme performance — journey L2, senior L3
- Supervise staff and volunteers in environmental work — senior L3
- Practise cultural humility in community, field and team work — journey L2, senior L3
- Conduct participatory and community-based environmental research — journey L2, senior L3

**Main tasks at this level (agent draft, in record order)**

*% time: set by the supervisor; EMST supplies none before job analysis.*

*Critical and needed-at-entry tasks: Assessment pending (job analysis).*

- Adapt restoration techniques at a site when monitoring shows plantings, structures or soils are not responding as planned, recording the change
- Read site response after a restoration treatment, such as sediment capture, wetting, establishment or browse, recording evidence at fixed photo points
- Build low-tech process-based structures such as beaver dam analogues or post-assisted log structures, placing each from field reading of flow and channel form
- Develop a restoration plan that accounts for the species interdependencies the target community needs to persist.
- Measure habitat attributes such as cover, structure, water and forage at used and available sites following a habitat-use study protocol
- Integrate habitat findings into land-use or project plans as specific measures that avoid or reduce effects on species of concern
- Determine whether restoration to historical conditions is feasible at a site, documenting the thresholds, drivers and costs that limit recovery
- Evaluate whether a site's vegetation, soils and disturbance regime have moved beyond the historical range of variability, citing field and record evidence
- Interpret fire scars, stumps, soil horizons and legacy structures at a site to reconstruct its disturbance and land-use history
- Reconcile field evidence of site history with maps, aerial photographs, management records and accounts from people who know the site
- Predict from site-history evidence where a planned treatment will meet legacy conditions, recording each prediction for comparison after treatment
- Define the monitoring questions, indicators and decision triggers for a plan or programme so that each indicator answers a stated management question.
